suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is read without optional chaining. WHY: when `evt.destinationCalendar` is an empty array (which this PR now produces in bookingReminder.ts, webhook.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts, confirm.handler.ts, editLocation.handler.ts, deleteCredential.handler.ts, requestReschedule.handler.ts) or nullish, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, so `undefined.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`, crashing booking creation for a Google Meet location with no destination calendar. This is a regression from the previous safe `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. HOW: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is evaluated only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never be true and always yields `undefined`. WHY: the previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`; now `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` and Google's update (line 261) / delete (line 317) falls back to 'primary' instead of the host's destination calendar, so updates/deletes hit the wrong calendar whenever no externalCalendarId is passed. Same defect at line 317 in deleteEvent. HOW: for the fallback select the destination calendar matching the credential/event, e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` (or match by the credentialId), not by comparing against the already-falsy `externalCalendarId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: for non-calendar results `credentialId` is now hardcoded to `undefined` (`credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`), whereas before it propagated `result.credentialId` for video events. WHY: the video BookingReference is persisted without a credentialId, and packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:491-501 locates the video credential via `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` to call `deleteMeeting`, so the video meeting is no longer deleted when a booking is cancelled. HOW: preserve the video credential id, e.g. `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` (i.e. just `result.credentialId`), matching how updateLocation still uses `result.credentialId ?? undefined` at line 209.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the subsequent collective-host calendars are merged with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op on `null`. WHY: for a COLLECTIVE event where the organizer has no destination calendar, the host destination calendars collected at lines 992-993 are silently discarded, so the multiple hosts are never invited — the exact scenario this PR is meant to fix. HOW: initialize the array before pushing, e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Unoptional-chained access to mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws when destinationCalendar is empty, a shape this PR now produces everywhere.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Removing the optional chain turns this into a runtime TypeError whenever destinationCalendar is empty. The old code `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` was null-safe; the new destructuring yields `undefined` for an empty/absent array, and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then dereferences undefined. Since the PR changes most callers (handleNewBooking, handleCancelBooking, stripe/paypal webhooks, confirm/editLocation/requestReschedule/deleteCredential handlers) to pass `[]` or `null`, processLocation now throws on those paths. Use optional chaining: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Null destinationCalendar makes the COLLECTIVE team-destination push a no-op, silently losing team calendar events.
suggestions.suggestionContent: destinationCalendar is now set to `null` when neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destinationCalendar, and the COLLECTIVE team calendars are appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. Optional chaining on a null array silently drops the push, so for a COLLECTIVE team event with no organizer/event-type destination calendar, every team member's destination calendar is discarded and no team calendar event is created — an invariant violation. Initialize to an empty array ([]) instead of null so the push always lands, or guard the push with an explicit array initialization.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: New loadUsers catch rethrows Prisma error.message (internal DB detail) to the API client.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new catch in loadUsers surfaces `error.message` to the caller for `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` (and HttpError). Prisma's known-request errors embed internal database detail — model/field names, unique-constraint field lists, and the failing query shape — which is now returned in the HTTP 400 response body. Prefer a fixed, non-revealing message for DB errors (e.g. log the real message server-side and throw a generic `{ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" }`), keeping only intentionally user-facing HttpError messages intact.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Destructuring index 0 of an empty/null `destinationCalendar` yields `undefined`, and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws a TypeError. The previous code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`). Since this PR makes empty arrays/null common, restore a guard: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: In the `else` branch `externalCalendarId` is guaranteed falsy, so `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can only match elements whose externalId is also falsy — it will essentially never find the intended destination calendar, and the old fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` was removed. Use the first destination calendar directly (e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`). The identical pattern at lines 315-317 in deleteEvent has the same defect.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` silently no-ops when `destinationCalendar` is `null` — which this function sets when neither the eventType nor the organizer has one (lines 1063-1067). In that case the collective team members' destination calendars gathered into `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped. Assign the merged array instead of relying on in-place push.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is the first element of `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it is `undefined` whenever destinationCalendar is null (handleNewBooking sets it to `null`) or an empty array (webhooks/confirm/editLocation/deleteCredential/handleCancelBooking now pass `[]`). Dereferencing `.integration` without optional chaining therefore throws a TypeError for these events. Before the PR this was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which defaulted the comparison to true and kept the Cal Video fallback working. Restore the optional chain (e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fallback that used to give the destination calendar's externalId is now dead code: this branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares against `undefined` and never matches, returning `undefined` instead of the destination calendar. Callers that previously updated the configured destination calendar will now address an undefined calendarId. Use the intended credential/externalId (e.g. the matching `mainHostDestinationCalendar` / `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]`), not a search keyed on the already-falsy `externalCalendarId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Same dead fallback in deleteEvent: `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it can never match and `calendarId` becomes `undefined` where it previously resolved to the destination calendar. The delete then targets an undefined calendar instead of falling back to the destination calendar.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The reference shape changed for non-calendar (video) results. Previously `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video references carried `result.credentialId`; now the expression is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, silently dropping credentialId from video references. Any consumer of `referencesToCreate` that relies on the video reference's credentialId loses it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: EventManager dereferences the first destinationCalendar element without optional chaining, but the PR's producer hunks now emit an empty array.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` was widened to `DestinationCalendar[]`, and the producer sites changed in this PR now build an empty array when no destination calendar exists (payments/api/webhook.ts:119, paypal-webhook.ts:154, confirm.handler.ts:176, editLocation.handler.ts:86, deleteCredential.handler.ts:291, handleCancelBooking.ts:252 all use `cond ? [x] : []`; handleNewBooking.ts:1064 uses `null`). In EventManager, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` dereferences the first element unconditionally. When the array is empty (or the field is null) the element is `undefined`, and for a Google Meet booking (`evt.location === MeetLocationType`) the `&&` short-circuit evaluates the second operand, throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and aborting calendar-event creation. Add optional chaining (or check `evt.destinationCalendar?.length`). The other consumers updated in this PR (googlecalendar:100/198, office365calendar:73, larkcalendar:128) all guard with `?.`/`?? []`; this one does not.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: New loadUsers HttpErrors expose hard-coded English messages instead of the translation keys used by the rest of the handler.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new error handling in loadUsers throws hard-coded English, user-facing messages: "dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty." (line ~727), "eventType.hosts is not properly defined." (line ~746) and "Unable to load users" (line ~761). Every neighbouring HttpError in this handler passes an i18n key instead (e.g. `throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 404, message: "eventType.notFound" })`), which the client resolves through the translation mechanism; these new plain-prose strings will be shown untranslated to the booker. Pass a translation key (or reuse the existing key / `error.message` pattern consistently with the rest of the handler) rather than raw English text.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Team admins are denied add-guests because isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner only accepts owners.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The authorization check combines `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)` with `&&`, but the two helpers test different role sets — `isTeamAdmin` returns truthy for ADMIN or OWNER, while `isTeamOwner` returns true only for OWNER (teams/index.ts:264-295). The `&&` therefore collapses the condition to "user is a team OWNER", so a team ADMIN always fails this predicate. WHY: A team admin who is otherwise allowed to manage bookings hits the `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` branch and receives a 403 `you_do_not_have_permission`, blocking a legitimate action — and this contradicts the sibling implementation, which uses `||` (confirm.handler.ts:127-128). HOW: change the operator to `||` so admins and owners are both accepted.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The error toast fallback is unreachable because the interpolated message is never falsy.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` always yields a non-empty string (e.g. "undefined: ..." when `err.data` is absent), so the fallback `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` is dead code. WHY: On any error where the server does not attach a `data.code`, the user sees a confusing literal "undefined: <message>" toast instead of the intended `unable_to_add_guests` message. HOW: build the message conditionally, e.g. only prefix the code when present and fall back to `t("unable_to_add_guests")` when the translation/message is missing.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Guest emails are compared to a lowercased blacklist without normalising the guest side, allowing a case-variant bypass of BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist is normalised to lowercase (line 71: `.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but the guest value is not: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Email is case-insensitive, so submitting `BLOCKED@Example.com` bypasses a blocklist entry of `blocked@example.com` and the address is still added to the booking and emailed. Normalise the guest side of the comparison, e.g. `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())` (or lowercase the whole `guests` array before filtering). For consistency the attendee-duplicate check at line 76 (`guest === attendee.email`) should be normalised the same way.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Duplicate-check reads a stale booking snapshot then inserts, so concurrent or duplicate-guest requests create duplicate attendee rows.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The duplicate check at 74-78 is a check-then-write against a snapshot fetched at 26-42, and the insert at 92-106 is a separate statement with no uniqueness guarantee. Two concurrent addGuests calls (or one call whose `guests` payload repeats an email, since the server schema does not dedupe) both pass the filter and both `createMany`, producing duplicate attendee rows. Rely on a DB-level unique constraint for attendees, or move the filtering into the write (e.g. upsert/skipDuplicates with a unique key, and dedupe the incoming array server-side with `new Set(guests)` before the filter).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Hard-coded English tooltip bypasses the translation mechanism used elsewhere in the same component.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The tooltip shown on the remove-email button is hard-coded English: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` (line 46). Every other user-facing string in this new component goes through the locale hook — the same file imports `useLocale` (line 1) and renders `t("add_another")` at line 69. This one string is therefore untranslatable and will render in English for all locales. Route it through `t()` with a corresponding key in the locale files, matching the pattern of the surrounding strings.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The thrown message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' is surfaced when the real condition is 'all guests already added/blacklisted', not invalid emails.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `uniqueGuests` (line 74) filters out addresses that already exist on the booking or are blacklisted, so `uniqueGuests.length === 0` means "none of the submitted emails is a *new* guest", not "the emails are invalid". The error message still claims `emails_must_be_unique_valid` ("Emails must be unique and valid") and is shown verbatim to the user by AddGuestsDialog (line 43-44 via `t(err.message)`). A user who submits perfectly valid, unique emails that are simply already attendees is told their emails are invalid. Use a message that describes the actual condition (e.g. a key such as `guest_already_exists` / `no_new_guests`) or distinguish the cases.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with `&&` although the name/intent is "admin OR owner", denying admins who are not owners.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never run because the template literal is always truthy.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `message` is built with a template literal and is therefore always a non-empty string, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is unreachable. If the intent is to fall back to a generic message when the server provides no usable error, decide on the error content explicitly instead of relying on the always-truthy literal.

suggestions.label: BUG
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: 审查 `isTeamAdminOrOwner`，该函数在第 46-48 行使用了 `&&` 而非 `||`。
suggestions.suggestionContent: 审计 `isTeamAdminOrOwner`，其第 46-48 行使用了 `&&` 而非 `||`，这被描述为布尔运算符/授权缺陷。

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Handler passes the raw input guests to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of the filtered uniqueGuests the consumer assumes.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler builds `uniqueGuests` (the emails actually added after removing emails already on the booking and blacklisted ones) and creates attendees only from those, but passes the raw `guests` input to `sendAddGuestsEmails`. The consumer `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525,541) treats its second argument as the set of newly-added guests and branches on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to pick `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Because the raw `guests` can contain emails that were NOT added (a re-submitted existing attendee or a blacklisted email), an existing attendee can match and wrongly receive a fresh scheduling/confirmation email. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The handler passes the raw guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, whose contract expects only the newly added guests (uniqueGuests).
suggestions.suggestionContent: The newly added `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` derives its recipient logic from `newGuests` (email-manager.ts: `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` -> AttendeeScheduledEmail, else AttendeeAddGuestsEmail), i.e. its parameter contract is "the guests that were actually just added". The handler already computes that set as `uniqueGuests` (lines 74-78: excludes attendees already on the booking and blacklisted emails) and uses it for the DB `createMany`, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the unfiltered input. Consequence: a guest email that was filtered out (already an attendee / blacklisted) is still classified as a new guest, so an existing attendee receives the plain `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the intended "new guests added" email. Pass `uniqueGuests` to keep the caller aligned with the function's contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `key` is assigned the whole safeParse result object `{ success, data }` returned by `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29 returns `refreshTokenResponse`, not `.data`) and persisted to the DB, whereas the previous code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` (the parsed credential). WHY: The stored key becomes `{success:true, data:{scope,token_type,...}}`, so the next construction's `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) cannot find `scope`/`token_type`/`expiry_date`/`access_token`/`refresh_token` and throws, breaking Google Calendar for that credential after every token refresh. HOW: use the parsed payload, e.g. `const parsed = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); const key = parsed.data;`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with `credentialId` (the credential's own id, set from `credential.id` at line 53) as its third parameter, but that parameter is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. WHY: When credential sharing is enabled the parent app receives the credential id instead of the Cal.com user id, so it looks up/refreshes credentials for the wrong (or no) user — every other caller in this PR passes `credential.userId`. HOW: pass `credential.userId` (thread it into `refreshAccessToken` or close over `credential`).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: In the credential-sharing branch `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15), but the code reads `res?.data` (axios/google-auth shape) and then `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date` on it. WHY: A `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` is `undefined` and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError; the surrounding try/catch treats it as a non-`invalid_grant` error and silently returns the unrefreshed auth, so Google Calendar token refresh never works in sharing mode. HOW: parse the response, e.g. `const token = APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED ? await res.json() : res?.data;` (or have the shared endpoint return the same shape).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` overwrites a missing `refresh_token` with the literal string `"refresh_token"` (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-26), and this parsed data is then spread over the stored credential at line 264 (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`). WHY: Microsoft's token endpoint does not always return a new `refresh_token`; when absent, the stored/valid refresh token is replaced by the placeholder literal, so every subsequent refresh fails and the credential is permanently broken. HOW: only merge real values, or make parseRefreshTokenResponse leave refresh_token untouched (or preserve `o365AuthCredentials.refresh_token` when the response omits it).

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Missing refresh_token is silently replaced with the literal string "refresh_token" instead of failing, corrupting stored credentials.
suggestions.suggestionContent: When the refreshed-token payload has no `refresh_token` field, the function mutates the parsed object and substitutes the hardcoded literal `"refresh_token"`. Callers persist this object directly (office365calendar/CalendarService.ts and salesforce/CalendarService.ts line 98), so a provider response that omits the refresh token will overwrite the user's real refresh token with a bogus constant, permanently breaking the integration and hiding the failure. Fail fast instead of supplying a placeholder credential value.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Webhook shared secret is compared with non-constant-time `!==`, leaking the secret via comparison timing.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The webhook secret from the request header is compared to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` using `!==`. JavaScript string inequality short-circuits on the first differing byte, so response time depends on how many leading bytes match the real secret. Because this endpoint authenticates anyone who knows the secret and then writes/overwrites credentials for an arbitrary userId, an attacker can recover the secret byte-by-byte. Use a constant-time comparison over equal-length buffers (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual`), rejecting length mismatches first.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParse wrapper, so the raw wrapper is persisted as the credential key, corrupting the stored Google credential.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the SafeParseReturnType object `{ success, data }`, not the parsed payload. Previously this line used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returned the flat token object. Now `key` is the wrapper and it is written straight to the DB via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. On the next refresh, `googleCredentials = credential.key` has no top-level `access_token`/`refresh_token`/`expiry_date`, so the credential is permanently broken. Unwrap the data (as the other callers do via `tokenResponse.data`).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: In the credential-sharing branch the helper returns the raw fetch Response while google-calendar/hubspot/zoho callers consume it as parsed token data, throwing on undefined access.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The sharing branch returns the raw `fetch` `Response`, but googlecalendar reads `res?.data` (and hubspot treats the result as a HubspotToken object; zoho-bigin/zohocrm read `tokenInfo.data.error`). In the non-sharing branch those same callers get the provider SDK's parsed object (`fetchTokens.res` has `.data`). So when sharing is enabled `res.data` is undefined and the next `token.access_token` access throws `Cannot read properties of undefined`. The helper must return the parsed body (e.g. `await response.json()` or a normalized `{ data: await response.json() }`) so the two branches are shape-compatible.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects the userId, sending the wrong identifier to the credential-sync endpoint.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `refreshOAuthTokens`'s third parameter is `userId: number | null` (used as `calcomUserId` in the sync payload and as the `&& userId` gate). Every other caller passes `credential.userId`; here `credentialId` (the credential's primary key) is passed instead, so the sync endpoint receives a credential id as the Cal.com user id. Pass `credential.userId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes the credential id where refreshOAuthTokens expects the Cal.com user id.
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId) declares and sends its third argument as the Cal.com *user* id (`calcomUserId: userId.toString()` in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:11). This caller passes `credentialId` (defined at line 53 as `credential.id`, the Credential row primary key), while every other caller in the PR passes `credential.userId`. When credential sync is enabled this sends the credential id where the sync endpoint expects the user id, so it looks up the wrong parent-application user. Pass the user's id instead of credential.id.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: google-calendar reads `res.data` from refreshOAuthTokens, which returns a Response on the sync path.
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response on the credential-sync path (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15), and the other consumers (office365, zoom, webex, lark) treat it as a Response by passing it to their `handleErrorsJson`/response helpers. Here `res` is then read as `res?.data` and `token.access_token`, a shape only produced by the in-process branch (`fetchTokens.res`). With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, `res` is a Response with no `.data`, so `token.access_token` throws. Parse the response body (or align the helper's return shape) on this path.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: refreshOAuthTokens documents its third parameter as a userId, but the zoho-bigin caller passes a credential id in that slot.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The signature is `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)` and the comment states the guard checks "that the credential belongs to a user", yet the zoho-bigin caller passes `credentialId` into this slot (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:93). Either the parameter/comment name is wrong or the caller is passing the wrong value; the name and the call site currently disagree, so a reader cannot tell which is intended. Align the parameter name/comment with what callers actually pass (or fix the caller).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: GoogleCalendar stores the SafeParse wrapper object as the credential key instead of the parsed data.
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParseReturnType ({success, data, error}), but this call site was previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`, which returned the parsed credential object directly. The result is now stored verbatim as the credential `key`, so the persisted key becomes `{success:true, data:{...}}` instead of the actual credentials. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` (or destructure `const { data: key } = ...`), matching the `.data` access used by the office365/zoom/salesforce consumers.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects the userId.
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId) defines its third argument as the cal.com *userId* (used as `calcomUserId` in the sync payload). Every other converted call site passes `credential.userId`; this one passes `credentialId`, a different identifier. Pass `credential.userId` so the credential-sync endpoint receives the user id it expects.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: parseRefreshTokenResponse changed from tolerant safeParse result to throwing, making caller failure branches dead and aborting formerly best-effort refreshes.
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" on a failed parse, whereas the call sites it replaced used safeParse and tolerated failure (office365calendar previously only console.error'd and continued). Callers that still contain `if (!tokenResponse.success)` branches (office365 line 264 context, salesforce line 92) are now unreachable, and a previously best-effort refresh can now abort the whole credential update. Confirm this behaviour change is intended for each caller, or return the failure and let callers decide.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Two computed keys collapse to the same string "[object Object]", so the number-typed expiry constraint is silently overwritten.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Both `[z.string().toString()]` (line 8) and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` (line 10) evaluate to the identical key `"[object Object]"`; object-literal duplicate keys keep only the last, so the `z.number()` expiry constraint on line 8 is silently dropped and only `access_token` is enforced. Use `z.record(...)`/`.catchall(z.unknown())`/`.passthrough()` instead of colliding computed keys.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Presence of refresh_token is tested by truthiness, so a legitimately falsy token is replaced with the literal "refresh_token".
suggestions.suggestionContent: `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token)` treats any falsy value as missing and overwrites it with the placeholder `"refresh_token"`; an empty-string token returned by the provider is silently replaced with a bogus value that is then persisted, breaking the next real refresh. Use an explicit existence check such as `=== undefined` or `"refresh_token" in refreshTokenResponse.data`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google stores the SafeParse wrapper object instead of parsed credential data as the credential key.
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns `refreshTokenResponse` (the whole `{success, data}` SafeParseReturnType), not `.data`. Every other caller unwraps `.data`, but google assigns the wrapper directly to `key` and writes it to the credential. The replaced `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the plain parsed object, so this persists `{success:true, data:{...}}` as the credential key, corrupting the stored credentials. Unwrap `.data` (or have parseRefreshTokenResponse return `refreshTokenResponse.data`).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` guard is unreachable because parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure.
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when `!success`, so if it returns at all, `success` is always true. The added `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) { return Promise.reject(...) }` can never run — a dead branch that gives a false sense of error handling. The check (and the reject) are unreachable.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId, sending the wrong calcomUserId.
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId) names its third parameter `userId` and forwards it as `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`. Every other call site (google, hubspot, lark, office365calendar, office365video, webex, zoom, zohocrm) passes `credential.userId`; zoho-bigin alone passes `credentialId`. If `credentialId` is the credential's id rather than the user's id, the sync endpoint receives the wrong `calcomUserId` and syncs the wrong credential. Pass `credential.userId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Shared-mode branch returns a fetch Response while google consumes the return as an object with .data.
suggestions.suggestionContent: In shared mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch `Response`. Consumers split: o365/zoom/webex/lark treat it as a Response (handleErrorsJson/`await resp.json()`), but google does `const token = res?.data; token.access_token` — a fetch Response has no `.data`, so the shared path yields undefined and reading `token.access_token` fails. The contract of the return value differs between the two branches and the google consumer. Return parsed JSON/data consistently (or have google handle the Response).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The JSDoc for createOAuthAppCredential documents both appData.type and appData.appId as "the app slug", but the code uses type as the credential type and appId as the slug.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
The doc block describes both fields as "the app slug":

 * @param appData.type the app slug
 * @param appData.appId the app slug

But in the body `appData.type` is written to `credential.type` (lines 49 and 63) while `appData.appId` is written to `credential.appId` (lines 52 and 66) — `type` is the app's credential type (e.g. `google_calendar`), not a slug. A caller reading the JSDoc would pass the slug in `type`. Fix the description for `appData.type`, e.g. `@param appData.type the app credential type (written to credential.type)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new `else` branch increments `retryCount` whenever `twilioProvider.scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value, but `scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` (without throwing) when the account is locked for SMS sending (`isLockedForSMSSending` true, twilioProvider.ts:92-95). WHY: A reminder whose send was skipped for a transient reason (account lock / rate limiting) is now treated as a send failure; after two cron runs `retryCount` exceeds 1 and the new top-of-handler `deleteMany` (lines 39-42) permanently deletes it — silently dropping legitimate reminders. HOW: Only increment retryCount on a real send failure (e.g. an exception from the Twilio call), and distinguish the locked/rate-limited skip from an actual failure, for example by having `scheduleSMS` signal a skip rather than returning undefined, or by not counting the skip in `retryCount`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `catch` block now performs an awaited `prisma.workflowReminder.update` that is not guarded by its own try/catch. WHY: If this update throws (transient DB error, row already deleted by a concurrent/previous deleteMany), the exception propagates out of the `for` loop, aborting processing of all remaining reminders and skipping `res.status(200).json(...)`, so the cron run fails midway. The previous code only logged and continued. HOW: Wrap the retry-increment update in its own try/catch so a failure to record the retry does not abort the whole batch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: retryCount is incremented for any error in the reminder loop, but it is also the field the cleanup deletes on, so unrelated errors can delete reminders that were never actually retried.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `retryCount` is incremented in the catch of the whole per-reminder try block, so it counts every failure (template rendering, getCalEventResponses, prisma.profile lookup, getBookerBaseUrl, and the final `workflowReminder.update` that persists referenceId), not SMS scheduling attempts. Because the same field drives the cleanup at lines 39-41 (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`), unrelated transient errors can exhaust the retry budget and delete a reminder whose SMS was never actually retried (e.g. the final update throws after Twilio already accepted the message). Narrow the increment to actual scheduling failures, or track the failure reason separately from the field used for deletion.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new retryCount increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write from a stale snapshot, so concurrent runs lose updates and reminders never reach the retryCount>1 abandonment threshold.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` is a read-modify-write on a value snapshotted once at fetch time (lines 48-60). Under overlapping cron invocations (or any duplicate trigger of this authenticated endpoint) two runs read the same snapshot (retryCount 0) and both persist 1, so an increment is lost. Since the deleteMany guard is `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` (lines 38-42), reminders whose increments are lost never reach the abandonment threshold and can be retried forever. Use an atomic increment so the counter cannot be clobbered:

```ts
data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } },
```

applying the same change to both the `else` branch (lines 179-186) and the catch block (lines 190-197).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The catch block now performs an unguarded awaited DB write, so a failure there aborts the whole reminder batch instead of being logged and skipped.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The error path used to be best-effort: `console.log(...)` and continue to the next reminder. Now the catch first does `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)`. If that update rejects (row concurrently deleted by another cron run, transient DB error, etc.), the rejection is not caught by this try and escapes the for-loop, so every remaining reminder in `unscheduledReminders` is skipped and the endpoint returns an error instead of 200. Wrap the retry-count increment so its failure cannot mask the original error and abort the batch, e.g. catch/ignore it, or move the increment into a helper wrapped in its own try. The original error should still be logged.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new OR disjunct drops the `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` guard, so the SMS cleanup now deletes rows of every reminder method from the shared table.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The added `OR` disjunct `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` carries neither `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` nor the `scheduledDate` bound that the original where-clause had. The SMS cron therefore now deletes rows for other methods (e.g. EMAIL reminders created by scheduleEmailReminders) that belong to other flows, and it does so with no date guard. Keep the scope explicit by repeating the method filter in the new branch (and/or the date bound) so the SMS cleanup can only affect SMS reminders: `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The comment above the deleteMany describes only the date condition, but the query now also deletes rows with retryCount > 1.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment at line 28 still says the delete only removes SMS reminders whose scheduledDate is in the past, but the where clause was changed to an OR that additionally deletes any reminder (any method, scheduled or not) with retryCount > 1. The comment no longer matches the code it documents — update it to mention the retryCount exhaustion branch so the next reader does not assume only past-dated SMS reminders are purged.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The retryCount delete branch is not scoped to SMS while the schema declares retryCount on all WorkflowReminder rows.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `retryCount` is declared on the shared `WorkflowReminder` table (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:1000; migration.sql:2), i.e. for every reminder method, whereas the SMS retry logic and the `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` guard in the sibling OR branch (lines 32-37) assume the `retryCount > 1` condition only ever matches SMS reminders. Because the `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` branch of the `OR` is not scoped by `method`, this `deleteMany` will delete ANY reminder (e.g. email reminders) once its `retryCount` exceeds 1, contradicting the schema's model-agnostic column vs this file's SMS-only intent. Hoist `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` out of the `OR` so both branches are SMS-scoped, matching the assumption the rest of the handler makes.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new backup-code branch authenticates on a valid backup code alone and never verifies the account password, because the only password check (line 121: `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`) is skipped whenever any non-empty totpCode is present. WHY: A crafted credentials request such as `{ email, password: "", totpCode: "000000", backupCode: "<valid code>" }` reaches line 131, matches the backup code, and returns success — granting a full login with the backup code as the sole factor, weakening 2FA to a single factor for anyone who obtains a backup code. HOW: reject the request when both `credentials.totpCode` and `credentials.backupCode` are supplied (or explicitly require the password to be verified for the backup-code path instead of relying on the `!credentials.totpCode` shortcut).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new required backupCode parameter of TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable was not applied to the older security/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx caller.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable` now requires a third `backupCode: string` argument (it is unconditionally serialized into the request body). The consumer apps/web/components/security/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:38 still calls `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable(password, totpCode)` with only two arguments, so it does not satisfy the new contract: TypeScript errors on the missing required parameter and the posted body omits `backupCode`. Update that call site (or make `backupCode` optional in the signature) so every consumer matches the new shape.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Backup-code verification compares the secret with indexOf (non-constant-time), leaking matches through timing.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The user-supplied backup code is validated with `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, a plain short-circuiting value comparison against secret codes. Array.prototype.indexOf stops at the first mismatch, so execution time leaks how many leading characters of a guessed code match a stored one, enabling byte-by-byte recovery of a valid backup code. Use a constant-time comparison over each candidate (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers, with a length guard) and check all entries without short-circuiting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The default export in this new file is named `TwoFactor`, but the module is `BackupCode` and it renders the backup-code field (t("backup_code"), placeholder XXXXX-XXXXX, register("backupCode")). Callers such as login.tsx and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx import it as `BackupCode from "@components/auth/BackupCode"`, so the function name contradicts both the file name and the call site, and reads as the TOTP TwoFactor component in stack traces/dev tools. Rename the function to `BackupCode` so the identifier matches what the code actually is.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Backup-code verification does a non-atomic read-modify-write, letting a one-time code be used twice under concurrent logins.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new backup-code branch decrypts `user.backupCodes`, checks membership, then nulls the entry and re-saves with `prisma.user.update`. There is no atomic guard: two concurrent authorize() calls presenting the same valid backup code both pass `indexOf(...) !== -1` on the same decrypted array and both persist it, so a code advertised as single-use (`backup_code_instructions`) is consumed twice. Make consumption atomic — e.g. a conditional `updateMany` that only succeeds while the stored ciphertext still equals the value read (optimistic compare-and-swap on `backupCodes`), or wrap the read/decrypt/consume in a transaction with a row lock — and reject when the conditional update matched 0 rows.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The copy test asserts only that a toast appears, so it passes even if the copy is broken.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The copy assertion does not test copying. In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx the success toast is shown unconditionally after a non-awaited `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)`, so `await page.getByTestId("toast-success").waitFor()` passes whether or not the clipboard write happened or contained the right codes. Assert the clipboard contents (grant clipboard permissions and `page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.readText())`, or intercept the clipboard call) and compare against the displayed backup codes, so removing/breaking `writeText` fails the test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The download test checks only a static filename, so it passes even if the downloaded payload is empty/broken.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The download assertion cannot fail for a broken payload. `cal-backup-codes.txt` is the static `download` attribute on the anchor (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx), independent of `href={backupCodesUrl}`; if the blob/URL construction is broken the anchor still downloads under the same name. Read the downloaded file and assert it contains 10 hyphenated codes so a broken download fails the test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: test4
suggestions.suggestionContent: test1

suggestions.label: state-reset issue
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: resetState fails to clear backupCodes and backupCodesUrl state.
suggestions.suggestionContent: resetState in EnableTwoFactorModal does not clear backupCodes/backupCodesUrl, so stale backup-code state remains after reset.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex but validated case-sensitively, so upper-cased input fails.
suggestions.suggestionContent: setup.ts:61 generates backup codes via `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, which is always lowercase. The validators at next-auth-options.ts:144 and disable.ts:61 compare `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` case-sensitively. Because the UI placeholder is uppercase (BackupCode.tsx:21 "XXXXX-XXXXX"), users typing the code in uppercase (or with any case change) get IncorrectBackupCode even though the code is correct. Normalize the user input at the validation sites, e.g. `const code = credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "").toLowerCase();` before `indexOf`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: resetState does not clear the backup-code state this PR added to the same component, unlike the sibling resetForm.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `resetState` resets password/errorMessage/step but not `backupCodes` (line 64) or `backupCodesUrl` (line 65), both introduced by this PR in this same component. The sibling reset in DisableTwoFactorModal (`resetForm`, DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:43-48) does clear every field it owns. As written, cancelling/closing after a successful setup leaves the old codes in state and keeps the blob URL alive until the next successful `handleSetup` (the only place it is revoked, line 98), so a reopened modal can still reference the previous codes/URL. Add `setBackupCodes([])` and revoke+clear the URL (e.g. `URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl); setBackupCodesUrl("");`) — also consider clearing `dataUri`/`secret`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The BackupCode component is declared as `function TwoFactor` (copy-paste from TwoFactor.tsx) although it renders the backup-code field.
suggestions.suggestionContent: This file was copied from TwoFactor.tsx and the component declaration was never renamed: the component renders a backupCode input and is imported as `BackupCode` in login.tsx:32 and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:8, but declares itself `function TwoFactor`. It works only because it is a default export; the stale name makes the declaration disagree with its actual use and will mislead anyone debugging which component registered the `backupCode` field. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: getBaseConditions contains unreachable fallback branches because authorization conditions are always present
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `else if (filterConditions)` and `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }` branches in getBaseConditions are unreachable because getAuthorizationConditions() is declared `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and buildAuthorizationConditions (lines 125-143) returns a Prisma.Sql on every path (never null/undefined). WHY: The deny-all fallback the author added for the 'no auth conditions' case can never trigger, so the code's actual contract (auth is always present) silently diverges from what this branch structure implies; a future change that makes buildAuthorizationConditions return null/undefined would be masked rather than handled, and a reader/test author is misled into believing an unauth path exists here. HOW: Either drop the dead fallback to make the invariant explicit (return authConditions/filterConditions directly, or assert authConditions is defined), or change the return type of getAuthorizationConditions to `Prisma.Sql | null` if absence is genuinely possible.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Removal of the Caching test block leaves the changed caching fields/accessors uncovered
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `describe("Caching")` block (two tests asserting that cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions are reused on the second call) was removed, and no replacement cover was added, even though this PR changes the type of both cached fields (insightsBooking.ts:49-50) and their accessors (84-95). WHY: The caching behavior that guards against recomputing/replacing authorization and filter conditions is now completely untested, so a regression that returns stale, wrong, or deny-all conditions on the second call would pass CI — the reference insightsRouting.integration-test.ts retains equivalent caching tests, so this suite is now weaker than its sibling. HOW: Re-add the two caching tests, updating the expected values to Prisma.sql form (e.g. compare `await service.getAuthorizationConditions()` on first and second call) instead of deleting them.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: getBaseConditions contains two unreachable branches because authConditions is a Prisma.Sql and thus always truthy.
suggestions.suggestionContent: getAuthorizationConditions() is typed to always return a Prisma.Sql (never null/undefined), so `authConditions` is always truthy. In getBaseConditions the `else if (authConditions)` branch therefore swallows every case not matched by the first `if`, making `else if (filterConditions)` (line 76) and the final `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION }` (line 79) permanently unreachable — dead branches left over from the where-object-to-Sql refactor. Since auth is always defined, the whole chain can be simplified to two cases, which also makes the intended semantics explicit. If the intent was really to allow authorization to be absent, the return type and builder would need to allow null — as written the fallback can never fire.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent:
WHAT: `i.content.scrub` calls `String#scrub`, which does not exist in Ruby 2.0 (added in Ruby 2.1).
WHY: The project targets ruby-2.0.0-p195 (.ruby-version.sample / .travis.yml), so this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub'` and, with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, kills the entire hourly feed-poll job — no feed posts are ever imported. Additionally, `i.content` is nil for feeds that only expose a `description` element (SimpleRSS maps `<content:encoded>` to `.content`), which would also raise on `nil.scrub`.
HOW: Replace with a Ruby-2.0-safe nil guard, e.g. `content = CGI.unescapeHTML((i.content || i.description || '').scrub)`, or drop `.scrub` and encode the string before inserting if needed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent:
WHAT: The template closes the `if/else` with `<%- end if %>`, which is invalid Ruby — `if` cannot be used as a modifier on the `end` keyword.
WHY: The ERB template fails to compile with a Ruby SyntaxError whenever `EmbedController#best` renders this view on the success path (topic found), so the primary embed output always errors instead of showing the discussion. The outer conditional at line 29 correctly uses `<% end %>`, highlighting the inconsistency.
HOW: Change line 6 to `<%- end %>`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Two poll_feed tests pass vacuously because feed_polling_enabled? defaults to false and short-circuits the guard.
suggestions.suggestionContent: PollFeed#execute guards with `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`. Tests "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" stub only their own setting but never feed_polling_enabled?, whose default is `false` (config/site_settings.yml). The first clause short-circuits and poll_feed is never reached, so both tests would still pass if the feed_polling_url / embed_by_username checks were removed. Fix: also stub feed_polling_enabled? to true and the other prerequisite settings to present so the clause under test is the one that stops execution.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: "is 404 without an embed_url" fails in the host filter, never reaching the embed_url requirement it names.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The controller's before_filter :ensure_embeddable (embed_controller.rb:4) raises Discourse::InvalidAccess when SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank? (line 25). This test never sets embeddable_host, so it is blank and the request fails in the filter before params.require(:embed_url) at line 9 executes. `should_not be_success` therefore passes for the missing-host reason, not the missing-parameter reason, and would still pass if the embed_url requirement were removed. Fix: set a host (and stubbed referer) so execution reaches the action and the parameter requirement is what produces the failure.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: AddCookMethodToPosts defaults cook_method to 1 (raw_html), so normal posts bypass the cook pipeline.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `Post.cook_methods` is `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, i.e. :regular = 0 and :raw_html = 1. The migration sets `default: 1`, which is the RAW_HTML value, so any post created without an explicit cook_method (the normal PostCreator path — see lib/post_creator.rb:216, which only assigns when the option is present) gets cook_method = 1 and then post.rb:133 `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` returns the unrendered raw text, skipping PostAnalyzer/Plugin::Filter entirely. The default must be the :regular value (0). Change to `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 0, null: false`. (Fix site is this migration; post.rb:63-65 declares the enum it must agree with.)

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: postMessage sender is authorized with a substring (indexOf) check instead of an exact origin comparison, allowing a sender whose origin is a substring of discourseUrl.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler accepts messages whenever `e.origin` is a *substring* of `discourseUrl` (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`). This is not an identity check: any origin contained anywhere in discourseUrl passes — e.g. host `https://discourse.example.co` passes when discourseUrl is `https://discourse.example.com`. Compare origins exactly; since discourseUrl may include a path, normalise both sides to origins before comparing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Non-atomic check-then-create on embed_url races with concurrent importers and raises an unhandled unique-constraint violation.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `TopicEmbed.import` selects with `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` (line 15) and only later does `TopicEmbed.create!` (line 25). The `topic_embeds` migration declares a UNIQUE index on `embed_url`, and nothing serializes the two steps. Two independent writers can reach this code concurrently for the same article: `EmbedController#best` enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job for every request that misses (embed_controller.rb:15), and the hourly `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every feed item (poll_feed.rb:36). `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` has the identical TOCTOU on `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` (topic_retriever.rb:37-42); its redis throttle only suppresses repeat retrievals of one URL by non-staff and does not protect against PollFeed running at the same time. Interleaving: A checks (no embed) → B checks (no embed) → A inserts → B calls `create!` → `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, which aborts the surrounding `Topic.transaction` and discards the topic/post A created, and the job fails with an unhandled exception. Make the path atomic: rescue `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and re-read the existing embed (treat it as the update path), or insert with an upsert (`find_or_create_by` inside a unique-constrained insert / `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT`) so the declared uniqueness is preserved instead of raising.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The request Referer header is interpolated unescaped into the embed layout's JavaScript, exposing the referer value in the response and allowing script injection.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `request.referer` is attacker-controlled and is written straight into the response body as a single-quoted JS string. Any referer containing a `'` (or `</script>`) breaks out and runs arbitrary script in the forum's origin; additionally the full referer URL (which may contain private query params/tokens) is echoed back in the response. Render it with proper encoding (e.g. `raw json_escape(request.referer.to_s)` / `escape_javascript` and, ideally, a validated origin), and ensure the value cannot terminate the string literal.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The migration default (1 = raw_html) contradicts the comment "Default is to cook posts".
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment added at app/models/post.rb:135 says "Default is to cook posts", but the migration sets `default: 1`. With `Post.cook_methods = Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` (post.rb:64), index 1 is `raw_html`, which the guard at post.rb:133 treats as "skip the rendering pipeline". The column's actual default is therefore the no-cook path, contradicting the comment and the intended default; posts created without an explicit `cook_method` would be left as unrendered raw HTML. Either the default should be 0 (`regular`) or the comment must change.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The migration defaults posts.cook_method to 1, which is `raw_html` in post.rb's enum, so every ordinary post skips cooking.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `Post.cook_methods` is `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` (post.rb:63-64), and Discourse's `Enum` is 0-indexed, so `regular == 0` and `raw_html == 1`. This migration sets the column default to `1` (`raw_html`), while `lib/post_creator.rb:216` only overrides `cook_method` when `@opts[:cook_method]` is present. So every post created without an explicit cook_method — all normal topics/replies — is stored as `raw_html`, and `Post#cook` (post.rb:133) hits `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, returning unrendered raw source and skipping `post_analyzer.cook` plus the `after_post_cook` filter. The default must be `regular` (0) so only imported/embedded posts use raw HTML rendering.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The resize postMessage uses request.referer (a full URL with a path) as targetOrigin, which browsers reject, so embed.js never receives the resize event.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The layout posts the resize event to the embedding page with `parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: ...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. The second argument of postMessage is a targetOrigin and must be an origin only (scheme://host[:port]); `request.referer` is a full page URL (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/article`, or nil), so the browser refuses to dispatch the message (Chrome throws `Invalid target origin`). The consumer in app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:15-24 (`postMessageReceived`) therefore never fires and the iframe never resizes to fit the embedded discussion. Pass a real origin (e.g. the origin derived from the embed URL, or `'*'`) instead of `request.referer`, or have embed.js send/handshake the expected origin.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Migration dereferences execute()[0] without a nil guard, crashing when no matching category row exists.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `execute("...")[0]['id']` assumes the category/embed_category join always returns a row; when it returns none, `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. WHY: On any site where `embed_category` is unset or no category matches its value (i.e. sites that never used embedding, including fresh installs), the migration aborts with a NoMethodError and the `if category_id == 0` fallback never runs. HOW: Mirror the guarded pattern used in db/migrate/20140715190552_remove_uncategorized_parents.rb, e.g. `row = execute(...)[0]; category_id = row && row['id'] ? row['id'].to_i : 0`, and apply the same guard to the uncategorized_category_id lookup on line 15.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: before_validation calls self.host.sub! without guarding nil host, crashing on blank input.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally in `before_validation`; if `host` is nil (create/update with a missing or blank `host` param), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError. WHY: The validation (validates_format_of) that would reject a blank host runs AFTER this callback, so a malformed request produces a 500 instead of a clean validation error; the client-side `cantSave` guard does not protect direct API calls. HOW: Guard the callback, e.g. `return if host.blank?` at the top of the before_validation block (Stub/Fabricate `EmbeddableHost.new` with host set is unaffected).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: update/destroy dereference a possibly-nil EmbeddableHost lookup.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil, and both `save_host(host)` (which does `host.host = ...`) and `host.destroy` then operate on nil. WHY: Any request with an unknown/already-deleted id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404-style error. HOW: Bail out when the lookup is nil, e.g. `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first; raise Discourse::NotFound unless host` in both update and destroy.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: host_allowed? lowercases only the column, so a case-differing referer/host fails to match.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` normalizes the stored column but not the bound value (`uri.host`), which Ruby's URI keeps in its parsed case. WHY: A referer or embed URL containing uppercase letters (e.g. `EvilTrout.com`) then fails to match a stored host, so a legitimate embed is rejected with 'invalid referer host'. HOW: Normalize the parameter too, e.g. `where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the embed_category lookup returns at least one row. When the `embed_category` site setting is absent or its value matches no category name, the SELECT yields zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError inside the migration instead of falling through to the `if category_id == 0` uncategorized fallback on line 14. Guard the result, e.g. `row = execute(...).first; category_id = row ? row['id'].to_i : 0` (and likewise for the uncategorized lookup on line 15), so the fallback actually runs when there is no match.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` on a value that may be nil. `save_host` assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly, so a missing/blank param makes `nil.sub!` raise NoMethodError (500) before the `validates_format_of` check can produce the intended validation error. Use a nil-safe form such as `self.host = self.host.to_s.sub(...)` (or guard with `self.host.present?`) so blank input fails validation cleanly instead of crashing.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Host allowlist lower-cases the DB column but not the input host, so mixed-case referers never match.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Inconsistent case normalization in a case-insensitive comparison. The query normalizes the stored side (`lower(host)`) but not the bind value: `host = uri.host` is passed as-is, and `before_validation` strips scheme/path but never down-cases. A referer with any upper-case host (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/...`) will not match the allowlisted `eviltrout.com`, so a legitimate embed is rejected. Normalize both sides, e.g. `where("lower(host) = ?", host.to_s.downcase)`. Note: this fails closed rather than granting access, so it is a correctness bug, not an authentication bypass.

suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: align-items mixin emits non-existent property -ms-align-items instead of a valid IE prefix.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a recognized CSS property (the IE10/IE11 prefix for align-items is `-ms-flex-align`, already emitted on the line above). WHY: The declaration is silently dropped by every browser, so it is dead code that indicates a prefix typo and could mislead future maintainers into trusting it as an IE fallback. HOW: Remove the `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` line (rely on the existing `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;`), or if a genuine IE fallback was intended, use `-ms-flex-align` only.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `order()` forwards the 0-based `order` value to the 1-based legacy `box-ordinal-group` properties, so prefixed ordering is shifted by one.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `order` / `-webkit-order` / `-ms-flex-order` are 0-based (unset elements are in group 0), but `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based (unset elements are in group 1). Passing `$val` straight through makes the legacy-prefixed layout disagree with the standard one: `@include order(1)` puts the element in the same ordinal group as every unset sibling, so old WebKit resolves the tie by source order and the item can render *before* the items it was supposed to follow. Emit `$val + 1` for the two `box-ordinal-group` declarations (or, for zero-padded output that is compatible across syntaxes, write `#{$val + 1}`). Current call sites (`order(3)` in header.scss:39, `order(2)` in topic.scss:30) happen to survive because both values exceed the legacy default group 1, but the shared mixin is now a trap for the next caller that needs `order(0)`/`order(1)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The align-items mixin writes the alignment value to `-ms-align-items`, a property no engine reads, duplicating the `-ms-flex-align` line above it.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `-ms-align-items` is not a property any engine recognizes (IE10's flex alignment property is `-ms-flex-align`, already emitted on the line directly above). The value passed to `@include align-items(...)` is written to this name and never read by any browser, so it is dead output that silently masks nothing but falsely suggests Microsoft support is covered by a second property. Drop the `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` line (or rename it to the property actually intended); the `-ms-flex-align` declaration above is the one that takes effect.

suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Two `self.downsize` definitions in the same class: the new (dimensions,opts) form silently overrides the (max_width,max_height,opts) form, making the latter unreachable and corrupting any width/height caller.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: totalPages uses floor(x/limit)+1 instead of ceil, creating a phantom extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit.
suggestions.suggestionContent: totalPages must be the count of non-empty pages: Math.ceil(user_count / limit). With offset-based paging, Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 over-counts by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (default limit is 50). Example: user_count=100, limit=50 yields totalPages=3, but the /groups/:name/members endpoint only returns two pages of results. Because showingLast = propertyEqual(currentPage, totalPages), on page 2 (currentPage=2) the next button stays enabled; clicking it sets offset = Math.min(50+50, 100) = 100, findMembers returns an empty member list, and currentPage then computes to 3 so the user is stranded on an empty '3/3' page with the next button now disabled. suggestions.label: bug

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Count-then-insert without a transaction lets concurrent requests exceed the configured anonymous device limit.

Two concurrent requests from two new device IDs when the store is at deviceLimit-1 will both read the same count and both insert, pushing the store over the configured limit. The ON CONFLICT (device_id) clause only dedupes the same device, it does not cap the total number of rows, so the invariant 'never more than AnonymousDeviceLimit active devices' is not actually guaranteed. Perform the count + insert inside a single transaction (or add a DB-level guard) so the limit holds under concurrency.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Success marker is cached before the DB write, so the new device-limit failure is cached as if the device had been tagged.
suggestions.suggestionContent: tagDeviceUI writes the success marker into the local cache before the DB write: `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` at line 87 runs unconditionally, and only afterwards CreateOrUpdateDevice is called at line 93. With the new ErrDeviceLimitReached path the DB write can now fail (for a device not already in the store while the limit is reached), but the positive cache entry is already present. For the next 29 minutes every request for that device ID hits the cache and returns nil without retrying, so the failure is cached under the key of the real answer and later readers silently get a 'tagged' result that never happened — the first request fails anonymous auth, subsequent ones succeed. Only set the cache entry after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, and delete it on the error path.

suggestions.label: bug

suggestions.label: bug

suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Removing the function-wide `b.cacheMu.Lock()`/`defer Unlock()` and locking only the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write removes the serialization that previously guaranteed a key is built once.
